common_name: Chabaud Giant Mix Carnation (Heirloom Fragrant Seed-Grown French Border Carnation)

planting.note: Start indoors six to eight weeks before the last frost, since Chabaud is a seed strain bred to reach florist-quality bloom in its first season; harden off and transplant after frost danger passes into well-drained, neutral-to-alkaline soil in full sun.

directions: Chabaud is a French heirloom carnation strain developed by breeder Jean Chabaud in the early 1900s, prized for producing fully double, intensely clove-scented blooms from seed in a single season rather than requiring the slower vegetative propagation typical of florist carnations. The mix opens in shades of scarlet, rose, white, salmon, and yellow on sturdy stems well suited to cutting, held above narrow blue-green foliage. Start seed indoors well ahead of the last frost for earliest bloom, then set plants into full sun and sharply drained, neutral-to-slightly-alkaline soil, pinching young plants once to encourage branching. Deadhead spent stems to extend flowering, and expect plants to persist as short-lived perennials in milder zones.

common_name: Grenadin Scarlet Carnation (Heirloom Fully-Double Single-Color French Border Carnation)

planting.note: Start indoors eight to ten weeks before the last frost, since Grenadin is a slow-to-bloom, large-flowered heirloom strain; harden off and transplant after frost danger passes into well-drained, neutral-to-alkaline soil in full sun.

directions: Grenadin Scarlet is the single-color scarlet selection out of the classic 19th-century French Grenadin border carnation strain, chosen where a uniform block of color is wanted rather than the mixed-color blend sold as Grenadin Mixed. It produces extra-large, fully double, spicy clove-scented flowers on strong stems above grassy blue-green foliage from early summer into fall. Sow indoors well ahead of the last frost, as Grenadin selections bloom later than modern bedding carnations, then transplant into full sun and well-drained, neutral-to-slightly-alkaline soil. Pinch young plants to promote branching and deadhead regularly to keep the display going, and expect worthwhile rebloom as a short-lived perennial in zones 6-9.

common_name: Amazon Rose Magic Dianthus (Color-Changing First-Year-Flowering Interspecific Sweet William)

planting.note: Direct sow or plant transplants in fall for spring bloom in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil in full sun; Amazon Rose Magic is an interspecific sweet william bred to flower the first year from an early seed start.

directions: Amazon Rose Magic is an interspecific Sweet William valued for flower clusters that change color as they age, opening bright white, aging through soft pink, and finishing an intense rose, so that all three shades appear together within a single cluster. Like other members of the Amazon series it flowers the first year from an early seed start instead of needing a full season of vegetative growth the way heirloom biennial sweet williams do, producing tall, sturdy stems well suited to cutting. Grow in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil, and deadhead spent clusters to prolong bloom through summer. It behaves as a short-lived perennial, generally performing best for two to three seasons before benefiting from renewal.

common_name: Amazon Neon Duo Dianthus (Bicolor Purple-and-Cherry First-Year-Flowering Sweet William)

planting.note: Direct sow or plant transplants in fall for spring bloom in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil in full sun; Amazon Neon Duo is an interspecific sweet william sold as a blend of the Neon Purple and Neon Cherry selections grown together.

directions: Amazon Neon Duo combines the two best-known Amazon series colors, Neon Purple and Neon Cherry, grown together as a blend so that dense, rounded flower clusters in glowing violet-purple and vivid cherry-red appear side by side in the same planting or bouquet. Like its parent selections it is bred to flower in its first year from an early seed start rather than needing a full season of vegetative growth, with individual florets carrying a light, sweet clove fragrance. Grow in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil, and deadhead regularly to keep both colors blooming from late spring into summer. It performs as a short-lived perennial, typically remaining vigorous for two to three years.

common_name: Scent First Sugar Plum Dianthus (Extra-Fragrant White-Edged Pink Garden Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Scent First Sugar Plum is part of the Whetman Pinks Scent First collection bred for strong clove fragrance on a compact mound.

directions: Scent First Sugar Plum produces ruffled, fully double flowers in vivid pink edged crisply in white, opening from dark, chocolate-colored buds that give striking contrast before the blooms unfurl. Part of the Whetman Pinks Scent First collection bred specifically for strong, sweet clove fragrance, it holds its narrow, bluish-green foliage in a tight, compact mound well suited to the front of a border or a container. Grow in full sun in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil, and deadhead spent blooms promptly to encourage repeat flowering from early summer into fall. It is more compact than many older garden pinks, making it a good fit for small spaces.

common_name: Scent First Passion Dianthus (Extra-Fragrant Velvety Red Compact Garden Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Scent First Passion is part of the Whetman Pinks Scent First collection bred for strong clove fragrance on a compact mound.

directions: Scent First Passion bears deep, velvety red, fully double flowers held on short stems above a dense cushion of blue-green foliage, one of the darkest-colored selections in the Whetman Pinks Scent First collection bred for intense clove fragrance. It flowers heavily in late spring and, with prompt deadheading of spent stems, continues to rebloom intermittently into fall. Grow in full sun in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil, since like all garden pinks it resents wet, heavy ground and benefits from a gritty topdressing in humid climates. Its compact habit suits raised beds, rock gardens, and the front of a sunny perennial border.

common_name: Rockin' Red Dianthus (Tall Vivid Red Interspecific Sweet William)

planting.note: Direct sow or plant transplants in fall for spring bloom in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil in full sun; Rockin' Red is a taller interspecific sweet william bred for durable, long-lasting color on sturdy stems.

directions: Rockin' Red is an interspecific Sweet William bred for taller, more vigorous habit than typical garden pinks, carrying dense clusters of vivid, true-red flowers on sturdy stems that stand well above the dark green foliage without flopping. It blooms over a long season from late spring into summer and reliably overwinters to USDA Zone 5, returning each year with reduced need for replanting compared to many annual bedding dianthus. Grow in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil, and shear lightly after the first flush to encourage a repeat round of bloom. Its height and sturdy stems make it useful in the middle of a perennial border as well as for cutting.

common_name: Rockin' Purple Dianthus (Tall Vivid Lavender-Purple Interspecific Sweet William)

planting.note: Direct sow or plant transplants in fall for spring bloom in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil in full sun; Rockin' Purple is a taller interspecific sweet william bred for durable, long-lasting color on sturdy stems.

directions: Rockin' Purple is an interspecific Sweet William grown for lacy, lightly scented flower clusters in a vivid lavender-purple, held on tall, full, long-lasting stems that make it a standout in perennial borders year after year. It reliably overwinters to USDA Zone 5, giving it more dependable multi-year performance than many annual bedding pinks, and blooms over an extended season from late spring into summer. Grow in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly alkaline soil, shearing lightly after the first bloom flush to tidy the plant and encourage repeat flowering. Its height and vivid color combine well with silver or chartreuse-foliaged companions in a sunny border.

common_name: Fruit Punch Cranberry Cocktail Dianthus (Proven Winners Hot Magenta-Pink Interspecific Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Cranberry Cocktail is part of the Proven Winners Fruit Punch series bred for improved heat tolerance and repeat bloom.

directions: Cranberry Cocktail, part of the Proven Winners Fruit Punch series, bears full, double flowers in a hot magenta-pink with heavily serrated petal edges, giving each bloom the look and spicy scent of a miniature carnation above a low, tidy mound of blue-green foliage. It flowers heavily in early summer and rewards a quick shearing after the first flush with a second round of bloom in early fall, showing good tolerance of summer heat and humidity compared to older garden pink cultivars. Grow in full sun in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil, since like other dianthus it performs poorly in wet or heavy ground. Its wide, low habit works well along border edges and in containers.

common_name: Fruit Punch Spiked Punch Dianthus (Proven Winners Fuchsia-Pink Red-Eyed Interspecific Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Spiked Punch is part of the Proven Winners Fruit Punch series bred for improved heat tolerance and repeat bloom.

directions: Spiked Punch, part of the Proven Winners Fruit Punch series, produces vibrant fuchsia-pink double flowers with a deep red eye and heavily serrated petal margins, the bold bicolor pattern standing out above a low mound of steel-blue foliage. It is drought, heat, and salt tolerant for a garden pink, attracting bees and butterflies while blooming heavily in early summer and again after a light post-bloom shearing. Grow in full sun in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil, as it needs sharp drainage to perform well through humid summers. Its compact, spreading habit suits edging, rock gardens, and mixed containers.
